newsitem.title: QATAR: Gulf Arab ministers meet, Bahrain boycotts talks.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arab ministers meet, Bahrain boycotts talks.

text.p: Gulf Arab foreign ministers met in Qatar on Wednesday to set the agenda for their leaders' annual summit but Bahrain boycotted the talks.
Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states Saudi Arabia, Oman, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates and host Qatar were due to meet again later on Wednesday to agree on the agenda for the summit on Saturday.
Qatar said Bahrain had turned down its invitation to attend the summit, which would be the first boycott since the political and economic alliance was formed in 1981.

The two states are locked in a border dispute over a cluster of islands and reefs which are potentially rich in oil and gas. Bahrain wants Qatar to withdraw the issue from the International Court of Justice in favour of a regional solution with Saudi Arabia mediation.

Summit agenda items include a review of steps taken in the past year towards achieving long-awaited economic integration, dealing with regional powers Iraq and non-Arab Iran, a rise in extremism and "terrorism" in the oil-rich region, and the Middle East peace process after fellow Arabs accused Israel of failing to honour signed accords.
